contracts.scope: Intel PIE startup graphs and bounded runtime dylib groups
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Mappings belong to loaded image groups. dlclose finalizes but retains mappings.
contracts.callbacks: Validate executable constructor/finalizer addresses; dependency-order construction and reverse teardown.
contracts.errors: Unsupported input fails before guest entry with worker exit125; guest exit codes preserved.
contracts.lifecycle: Resolve imports before mapping; relocate all images before constructors; join owned threads before unmapping.
contracts.unsupported: No shared cache, weak coalescing, dynamic TLV or dynamic Objective-C registration.

contracts.scope: C/POSIX locale, stream/format and jq/ripgrep-oriented POSIX adapters
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Guest FILE and host CRT stream are separate objects; never pass guest stat/tm/va_list to CRT.
contracts.callbacks: printf entry assembly captures SysV registers; no guest callback escapes the declared ABI.
contracts.errors: Per-thread Darwin errno; explicit ENOTSUP paths; errno mapping remains partial.
contracts.lifecycle: Session owns stream/environment state and flushes at exit; fopen/fclose manage individual streams.
contracts.unsupported: No Unicode locales, cookie streams, positional/wide/80-bit formatting or complete POSIX metadata/timezones.

contracts.scope: TLV, pthread lifecycle, keys, once, synchronization subset and the public static-initializer layouts
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Runtime owns thread tokens and per-thread storage; mutex/condition host objects are process-local.
contracts.callbacks: Start routines, key destructors and TLV destructors are SysV64; teardown permits bounded destructor re-registration.
contracts.errors: pthread APIs return Darwin error numbers; condition timedwait uses absolute guest deadlines.
contracts.lifecycle: Join owned threads before mapping teardown; run thread-local destruction and main-session cleanup.
contracts.unsupported: No cancellation, process-shared waiting, shared-cache TLV, robustness or scheduling-policy attributes, and no complete Darwin ordering proof; the same-binary suite covers the synchronized families only.

contracts.scope: Simple messages and bootstrap routing in local/broker namespaces
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Names refer to worker-owned rights; broker routes global endpoints and retires disconnected peers.
contracts.callbacks: Synchronous message APIs; no arbitrary host pointer or kernel handle passed as a guest right.
contracts.errors: XNU-style send/receive errors, header inversion, timeout and LARGE retry for supported operations.
contracts.lifecycle: Allocate/insert/deallocate within the owning namespace; send-once consumed; death invalidates routes.
contracts.unsupported: No complex/OOL/port descriptors, port sets, kernel enforcement, notifications or task APIs.

contracts.scope: Non-ObjC Blocks and Adapter-defined typed XPC between workers
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Copied handler blocks and typed objects are retained/released by runtime; no guest pointer serialized.
contracts.callbacks: SysV invoke on dispatcher thread; copied handlers remain alive through queued dispatch.
contracts.errors: Missing services and disconnected peers yield invalid/interrupted connection events.
contracts.lifecycle: Listener check-in, accepted peers, sync reply, cancellation and peer retirement are bounded implemented paths.
contracts.unsupported: No Apple wire interoperability, GCD/xpc_main, richer handles, ObjC captures, entitlements or security boundary.

contracts.scope: Five immutable runtime-created UTF-8 string functions
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Opaque runtime-owned strings; CF retain/release only for admitted objects.
contracts.callbacks: No callback-based collection or allocator interface exposed.
contracts.errors: Unsupported encoding or insufficient conversion space returns the implemented failure result.
contracts.lifecycle: Session owns the string registry; explicit retain/release changes references.
contracts.unsupported: No constant CF strings, collections, toll-free bridge, Foundation or runloop.

contracts.scope: Validated raw-isa manual-reference-counted startup images with relative method lists and startup categories
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Runtime-owned instances, counts and explicit balanced autorelease pools; no custom RR interception.
contracts.callbacks: msgSend preserves SysV GP/SSE/stack arguments and tail-jumps; superclass-first load and lazy initialize run outside registry lock.
contracts.errors: Validate metadata before selector patching or constructors; unknown selector terminates125.
contracts.lifecycle: Register complete startup graph, load before C constructors; guard remains live through guest finalizers.
contracts.unsupported: No protocols/properties/ARC/weak/tagged pointers/nonpointer isa/direct-selector or shared-cache lists/dynamic registration/exception or aggregate-return dispatch.

contracts.scope: Mach VM allocation, release and protection for the guest's own task
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; mach_vm_address_t and mach_vm_size_t are 64-bit, kern_return_t is a 32-bit int, task ports are 32-bit names.
contracts.ownership: An allocation is a host reservation recorded by the runtime; only recorded ranges are releasable.
contracts.errors: KERN_SUCCESS 0, KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS 1, KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE 2, KERN_NO_SPACE 3, KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT 4; task ports other than mach_task_self are refused.
contracts.lifecycle: Regions live until released or the run ends; release returns the host reservation to the operating system.
contracts.unsupported: No region queries, sharing, sub-range release, inheritance, ledger accounting, copy/read/write or purgeable flags.

contracts.scope: Synchronous Darwin signal dispositions, masks, raise/kill on the guest's own pid and default termination
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; sigset_t is a 32-bit mask with bit (signal - 1); handlers take (int) or (int, siginfo*, ucontext*) and are called with the latter two null.
contracts.ownership: Handler addresses are guest code; the adapter stores them and never frees or relocates them.
contracts.callbacks: Handlers run synchronously on the calling guest thread's stack with the signal and sa_mask blocked.
contracts.errors: EINVAL for signal 0, out of range, SIGKILL/SIGSTOP dispositions and unknown sigprocmask how; ESRCH for foreign pids; EPERM for pid -1; SIG_ERR from signal.
contracts.lifecycle: Dispositions and the mask live for the run; an unhandled terminating signal exits with 128 + signal.
contracts.unsupported: No asynchronous delivery, per-thread masks, siginfo/ucontext, sa_flags, alternate stacks, fault mapping, pthread_kill or sigwait.
